table_title: List 22 historically notable robotic (uncrewed) spacecraft missions of the Space Age — drawn from Wikipedia's 'Timeline of artificial satellites and space probes' master article — with each mission's launch year, primary destination, and final or current mission outcome. Crewed Apollo missions are excluded (covered by the sibling instance `apollo_lunar_landing_mission_crews`).
db_analog: SELECT m.mission_name AS mission, m.launch_year, m.primary_destination AS destination, m.final_or_current_outcome AS outcome FROM spacecraft_missions m WHERE m.is_robotic = TRUE AND m.is_notable = TRUE ORDER BY m.launch_year ASC, m.mission_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'Timeline of artificial satellites and space probes' master article + 22 per-mission Wikipedia articles, all accessed 2026-05-13. The universe is 22 historically notable robotic (uncrewed) spacecraft missions spanning the Space Age (1957-2021), curator-selected from the master article's full multi-decade enumeration to cover all three eras (Space Race 1957-1972, post-Apollo 1972-1996, modern 1996-present) and all primary-destination buckets the staged set uses (Earth Orbit, Moon, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Outer Solar System, Sun, Sun-Earth L2). Crewed Apollo missions are excluded (covered by sibling instance `apollo_lunar_landing_mission_crews`). Outcome values follow per-mission Wikipedia article framing: Success (mission objectives met per article lead and/or master-timeline outcome marker; mission ended via planned end-of-life or expected decay), Ongoing (mission still operating as of the source-access date — applies to Voyager 1/2, Hubble, New Horizons, Curiosity, Parker Solar Probe, Perseverance, James Webb). The Outcome enum also declares Partial success and Failure values for future-cycle expansion, but no row in the staged 22-mission universe uses them — all 22 are Success or Ongoing per master-timeline and per-mission-article framing. temporal_sensitivity = medium because the Ongoing rows may transition to Success (planned end-of-life) over the next 5-10 years. Launch year is current as of source access; no in-flight missions in the staged set have changed launch year (a few have updated outcome since launch — e.g., Cassini ended in 2017, Opportunity ended 2018, Spirit ended 2011).
_extraction_notes: Multi_hop instance: per-mission lookup requires resolving multiple chained attributes from the per-mission Wikipedia article (mission → launch metadata for Launch Year; mission → primary-target description for Destination; mission → end-of-mission section or 'current status' field for Outcome). Each attribute is sourced from a different part of the article (lead/infobox/body/end-of-mission section), making per-row retrieval a multi-step process. Universe = 22 curator-selected notable robotic spacecraft missions from Wikipedia's 'Timeline of artificial satellites and space probes' master article (which lists hundreds of missions across all eras). Schema: 4 cols (Mission PK + Launch Year numeric + Destination categorical + Outcome categorical). Tour distribution by era: Space Race (1957-1972) 8 rows, post-Apollo (1975-1996) 6 rows, modern (1997-2021) 8 rows — balanced across eras. Destination distribution: Mars 8, Earth Orbit 2, Moon 2, Venus 2, Outer Solar System 3, Jupiter 2, Saturn 1, Sun 1, Sun-Earth L2 1 (9 distinct values in staged data; declared enum also covers Mercury and Comet/Asteroid for the broader vocabulary even though no row uses them). Outcome distribution: Success 14, Ongoing 8 (2 distinct values used; Partial success and Failure are in the declared enum but not staged — all 22 selected missions either succeeded or are ongoing per master-timeline + per-mission-article framing). Sort: Launch Year ASC primary, Mission ASC secondary. Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + extinctions-cycles + deserts-cycles + tennis-cycles + music-genres-cycles + olympians-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Mission (Wikipedia common-form name with parenthetical disambiguation stripped where unambiguous — e.g., 'Galileo' rather than 'Galileo (spacecraft)', 'Curiosity' rather than 'Curiosity (rover)'); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles (master + per-mission); (c) explicit selection rule for Destination (primary target per per-mission Wikipedia article's lead — Voyager 1/2 → 'Outer Solar System' because their primary scientific objective spans Jupiter/Saturn/(Uranus/Neptune)/interstellar; Pioneer 10 → 'Jupiter' per its lead's 'first mission to the planet Jupiter' framing); (d) explicit Outcome rule (Wikipedia-lead foregrounded final or current state; Ongoing if the article uses present tense for current operation); (e) partially_supplemented universe (22 of N missions in the master article; Apollo crewed missions excluded as sibling-instance overlap); (f) crewed/uncrewed boundary explicitly committed (Apollo Moon landings = crewed, sibling instance; all 22 staged rows are uncrewed/robotic).
